evidence: The dictionary names all 33 variables and the live codes are those names with the wave prefix stripped; the sets are identical. Tested against a prediction the data could refute, since the renaming happened upstream of this repo: each code's observed waves must equal the set its b_/e1_/e2_ prefixes imply. 12 of the 33 are wave-restricted and therefore discriminating, and all 12 hold -- nine baseline-only codes (comp1-4, let_fill*) appear at wave 0 alone and three endline-only codes (word_dic1-3) never appear there, while the other 21 span all three waves. A permutation of the restricted codes against the all-wave ones would have shown a code at a wave its item did not exist in; none does. PARTIAL: the route does not separate all-wave codes from each other or task-family members from each other, and item_text is a task description rather than a literal item -- necessarily so for the nine picture-dependent items, which have no transcribable stem at all. Item sets match at 33, resp sets at 0/1.

The dictionary names all 20 variables and the live codes are those names with the wave prefix stripped; the sets are identical. Because the renaming happened upstream of this repo it was tested against a prediction the data could refute: each code's observed waves must equal the set its b_/e1_/e2_ prefixes imply. 19 of 20 codes are defined in all three waves, so this table has only ONE discriminating code and the route is correspondingly weak -- stated plainly rather than dressed up. That one code, add2d_b, came out as a mismatch and the cause is a typo in the dictionary, not in the mapping: End1 row 8b gives the variable name as e1_mathwrit_std12_add2d_a, duplicating row 8a, while its question label correctly reads q8_b. The data has add2d_b at midline, so the data is right. Harmless for what ships, since rows 8a and 8b carry the identical task description. PARTIAL: the route does not separate all-wave codes from each other or task-family members from each other, and item_text is a task description rather than a literal item. Item sets match at 20, resp sets at 0/1.

Two routes, because the wave route that verified the other Banerjee tables has no power here -- every code appears at both waves. ROUTE 1, the correspondence: haryana_analysis.dta labels these variables with the question number only, and the study's UTK/BH dictionary supplies what each question number asks. The two sets match exactly at 30 codes, and idiosyncratically -- the Hindi numbering runs 1.1 to 11.2b including 9.1a and 9.2b, the math 1a to 14c including 12a-12e -- so a different instrument would not share the structure. ROUTE 2, difficulty clustering: items sharing a task description are the same task, so their proportion-correct should cluster, and a wrongly attached set of descriptions would destroy that. 14 task families, 7 with more than one item. Mean within-family variance of p-correct is 0.01257 observed against a permutation null (4000 draws) of mean 0.04239 and MINIMUM 0.00974 -- the observed value falls below the null's minimum -- giving p = 0.0010. The per-family difficulty ordering also reads correctly by hand, with comprehension and division hardest. PARTIAL for two reasons: within a task family the items are interchangeable on this evidence, and no Haryana test instrument is deposited, so that Haryana used the identical printed form is inferred from the question numbering rather than shown. Item sets match, resp sets at 0/1.
